documents.title: Valve Machining Center Cooling & Temperature Alarm Procedure
documents.summary: Standard operating actions to reduce temperature and inspect cooling pump for valve machining centers.

pages.text: This work instruction defines mandatory corrective actions when spindle or machining chamber temperature exceeds 70°C in the Valve Machining Center (VMC-400-A).

When valve machine temperature reaches or exceeds 75°C: 1. Check the coolant flow and inspect the cooling system. 2. Reduce the machine load and monitor the temperature. 3. Inspect coolant filters for swarf buildup and ensure reservoir level is above minimum line. 4. If temperature remains high, follow the approved cooling procedure and notify shop supervisor.
At 90°C thermal alarm trip, machine executes automatic spindle feed hold. Do not attempt manual bypass. Verify external auxiliary chiller circulation.

chunks.text: Check the coolant flow and inspect the cooling system. Reduce the machine load and monitor the temperature. If it remains high, follow the approved cooling procedure.

documents.title: CNC Valve Turning Lathe Startup & Calibration SOP
documents.summary: Standard morning startup checklist and axis zeroing procedure for CNC Valve machine.

pages.text: 1. Turn on main isolator switch on rear cabinet. 2. Release emergency stop button and wait for CNC controller boot. 3. Perform home position reference return on X and Z axes. 4. Verify hydraulic pressure gauge reads 45 ± 2 bar before chuck clamping.

documents.title: Valve Hydraulic Filter Replacement Work Instruction
documents.summary: Step-by-step instructions for hydraulic and coolant return filter cartridge replacement.

pages.text: Isolate electrical feed (LOTO). Depressurize hydraulic reservoir via manual bleeder valve. Unscrew filter canister using tool wrench W-32. Inspect O-ring seal for nicks. Install replacement micron cartridge (Part V-FLT-88) and torque housing to 35 Nm.

chunks.text:
1. Apply Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) to hydraulic power pack.
2. Depressurize the reservoir using the manual bleed valve.
3. Remove filter bowl with wrench W-32 and extract old cartridge.
4. Clean housing, lubricate new O-ring with hydraulic oil ISO VG 46.
5. Insert new cartridge (Part V-FLT-88) and torque to 35 Nm.

documents.title: High Pressure Hydrostatic Valve Shell Testing Protocol
documents.summary: API 598 hydrostatic shell and seat leak testing standard parameters.

pages.text: Clamp valve body securely in test fixture. Fill cavity with demineralized water ensuring air vent is open. Pressurize to 1.5x design rating (350 bar) and hold for 180 seconds. Check gland packing and body joint for zero visible leakage.

chunks.text:
1. Secure valve body in the hydraulic test bench fixture.
2. Fill completely with test water while venting entrapped air.
3. Ramp pressure up to 350 bar at 10 bar/sec rate.
4. Hold pressure for 180 seconds and inspect seal perimeter for zero seepage.

documents.title: Centrifugal Pump Pressure & Flow Verification Protocol
documents.summary: Standard method to check pump pressure, head, and cavitation thresholds.

pages.text: How should the pump pressure be checked: 1. Confirm suction isolation valve is 100% open to prevent cavitation. 2. Verify pressure gauge calibration sticker is within valid date. 3. Start motor and run at nominal speed for 2 minutes to stabilize. 4. Record discharge gauge reading across closed and open discharge throttling positions (nominal: 120 ± 5 bar).

keywords: how should the pump pressure be checked
chunks.text:
1. Ensure suction valve is fully open to avoid cavitation.
2. Inspect calibrated digital manometer at discharge port.
3. Run drive motor for 2 minutes at rated RPM to stabilize.
4. Check discharge pressure reads 120 ± 5 bar across nominal flow.

documents.title: Pump Mechanical Seal & Impeller Alignment Guide
documents.summary: Assembly instructions for dual cartridge mechanical seals and impeller dial-indicator alignment.

pages.text: Mount dial indicator on shaft collar. Rotate shaft by hand and check radial runout is under 0.03 mm. Set seal spring compression using gauge spacer.

chunks.text:
1. Mount magnetic base dial indicator on drive shaft.
2. Measure radial runout (< 0.03 mm allowed tolerance).
3. Position cartridge seal clips and torque gland nuts evenly in criss-cross pattern.

documents.title: Industrial Gearbox Inspection & Dynamic Testing Procedure
documents.summary: Comprehensive gearbox inspection, bearing acoustic measurement, and backlash verification.

pages.text: What is the gearbox inspection procedure: 1. Isolate main drive motor and lock disconnect switch. 2. Visually inspect casing and split joints for lubricant seepage. 3. Check oil level via sight glass and examine magnetic drain plug for metal flakes. 4. Measure tooth contact pattern using Prussian blue and record backlash across 4 quadrants (tolerance: 0.035 - 0.050 mm). 5. Monitor bearing vibration and thermal profile during 30-minute no-load test.

keywords: what is the gearbox inspection procedure
chunks.text:
1. Isolate gearbox drive and engage safety lockout.
2. Inspect casing seals and split joints for oil seepage.
3. Check oil level in sight glass and inspect magnetic sump plug.
4. Measure gear tooth backlash across 4 quadrants with dial gauge.
5. Run test cycle to verify bearing acoustic vibration is under 1.8 mm/s.

documents.title: Gearbox Auxiliary Cooling Pump Replacement Procedure
documents.summary: Replacement steps for Gearbox Cooling Pump (Part No. GCP-204).

pages.text: Equipment: Gearbox Cooling Pump (Part No. GCP-204). Replacement procedure: 1. Isolate power supply and tag breaker. 2. Drain coolant into clean disposal drum. 3. Remove mounting flange bolts. 4. Install new replacement pump and check shaft coupling alignment. 5. Refill coolant to marked level and perform 10-minute leak-check run.

documents.title: Heavy Structural Welding PPE and Pre-Heating Standard (ASME Sec IX)
documents.summary: Safety requirements, mandatory PPE, and preheat temperature verification for submerged arc welding.

pages.text: What PPE is required during welding: 1. Auto-darkening welding helmet (Shade DIN 10-12 minimum). 2. Flame-retardant split leather welding jacket and heavy-duty split cowhide gauntlet gloves. 3. Steel-toe safety boots with metatarsal heat guards (EN ISO 20345). 4. Clear safety glasses with UV side shields worn under the helmet. 5. Fume particulate respirator (P3/FFP3 rated) in confined fabrication bays.

keywords: what ppe is required during welding
chunks.text:
1. Auto-darkening welding helmet (Shade DIN 10–12).
2. Flame-retardant split leather jacket and gauntlet gloves.
3. Steel-toe safety boots with metatarsal protection.
4. Clear UV-filtering safety glasses worn beneath helmet.
5. FFP3 fume extraction respirator in closed bays.

documents.title: CNC Plasma Torch Height & Bevel Cut Setting Calibration
documents.summary: Arc voltage control and pierce delay settings for 40mm carbon steel plates.

pages.text: Verify initial height sensor (IHS) ohmic contact. Set pierce height to 7.0 mm with 1.8 second delay before dropping to 3.5 mm cutting height at 260 Amps.

chunks.text:
1. Calibrate ohmic initial height sensing probe.
2. Set pierce height to 7.0 mm with 1.8s dwell time.
3. Transition torch to 3.5 mm cutting distance at 260 A.

documents.title: Medium Voltage Electrical Panel Dielectric & Insulation Testing SOP
documents.summary: Step-by-step dielectric high-potential (Hi-Pot) and insulation resistance testing standard (IEC 61439-1).

pages.text: How should the electrical panel be tested: 1. Confirm panel main incomer breaker is racked out and disconnected. 2. Verify all sensitive electronic PLC cards and surge arresters are unplugged or bypassed. 3. Perform 1000V Megger insulation resistance test (must exceed 100 MΩ). 4. Apply 2.5 kV AC dielectric test between phases and earth for 60 seconds. 5. Discharge busbars completely to earth before handling.

keywords: how should the electrical panel be tested
chunks.text:
1. Rack out and lock the main incomer circuit breaker.
2. Disconnect or bridge sensitive PLC controllers and surge suppressors.
3. Conduct 1000V DC Megger test (minimum 100 MΩ requirement).
4. Apply 2.5 kV AC Hi-Pot test for 60 seconds between phases and earth ground.
5. Discharge all stored capacitive charge to ground before touching.

workInstructions.title: Draft Work Instruction: Replacing the valve filter
workInstructions.purpose: Standard operating sequence for replacing the valve filter. Requires supervisor approval prior to shop-floor execution.
safety: Wear mandatory eye protection and thermal/chemical gloves.
procedure: Isolate electrical power and depressurize system.
Extract old component and inspect sealing surfaces for damage.
Fit replacement part and torque to approved specification.
Conduct slow pressure ramp test and check for weeping.
completion: Update maintenance logbook and return safety key.

workInstructions.title: Draft Work Instruction: Valve Filter Cartridge Replacement
workInstructions.purpose: Routine replacement of return-line hydraulic filter element to ensure uninterrupted coolant filtration.
safety: Isolate electrical power and apply Lockout/Tagout (LOTO).
Verify hydraulic gauge indicates 0 bar residual pressure.
Wear nitrile protective gloves and safety spectacles.
procedure: Position collection tray directly beneath filter housing.
Open manual depressurization valve to vent tank pressure.
Unthread filter canister using wrench W-32.
Extract depleted filter element and inspect housing bowl for swarf particulates.
Lubricate replacement seal ring with clean ISO VG 46 oil and fit new cartridge (V-FLT-88).
Hand-tighten canister until sealed, then torque to exactly 35 Nm.
inspection: Perform 5-minute pressure cycle test and inspect canister mating seam for weeping.
completion: Log cartridge batch code in machine logbook and remove LOTO tag.
